section_title: Section 1: Lumbar Spine Magnetic Resonance Imaging (CPT-72148)
text:
Clause 1.1: Clinical Indication Overview
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the lumbar spine without contrast (CPT-72148) is considered medically necessary only when conservative medical management has failed or when specific neurologic red flag indications are met.

section_title: Section 1: Lumbar Spine Magnetic Resonance Imaging (CPT-72148)
text:
Clause 1.2: Conservative Therapy Requirement
Authorization requires documented failure of at least six (6) continuous weeks of provider-directed conservative therapy within the preceding six (6) months. Conservative therapy must include at least one of the following:
- Formal physical therapy notes documenting active exercise rehabilitation.
- Prescribed NSAID or non-opiate analgesic medication regimen.
- Activity modification and chiropractic or home exercise progression supervised by a licensed practitioner.

section_title: Section 1: Lumbar Spine Magnetic Resonance Imaging (CPT-72148)
clause_title: Neurologic Red Flag Exceptions (Exempt from 6-Week Rule)
text:
Clause 1.3: Neurologic Red Flag Exceptions (Exempt from 6-Week Rule)
Prior authorization is approved immediately without conservative therapy trial if documentation establishes ANY of the following:
- Cauda equina syndrome (bowel/bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia).
- Rapidly progressive motor deficit (grade 3/5 or less muscle strength on manual muscle testing).
- Suspicion of spinal infection (fever, elevated inflammatory markers ESR/CRP, recent bacteremia).
- Known active malignancy with new onset unremitting back pain.

section_title: Section 1: Lumbar Spine Magnetic Resonance Imaging (CPT-72148)
text:
Clause 1.4: Required Evidence Submission Checklist
The ordering provider must submit:
1. Complete clinical examination notes including dermatomal sensory and motor grading.
2. Signed physical therapy completion notes or detailed rehabilitation discharge summary.
3. Relevant prior plain radiograph (X-ray) reports completed within the last 12 months.

---

section_title: Section 2: Knee Magnetic Resonance Imaging (CPT-73721)
text:
Clause 2.1: Clinical Indication Overview
MRI of the lower extremity knee joint without contrast (CPT-73721) is medically necessary for evaluating suspected internal derangement, meniscal tear, or ligamentous injury.

section_title: Section 2: Knee Magnetic Resonance Imaging (CPT-73721)
text:
Clause 2.2: Conservative Management Criteria
Except for acute high-energy trauma, authorization requires:
- Documented failure of four (4) weeks of conservative therapy (rest, NSAIDs, physical therapy, or unloader brace).
- Persistent joint line tenderness, effusion, or mechanical symptoms (locking, catching).

section_title: Section 2: Knee Magnetic Resonance Imaging (CPT-73721)
text:
Clause 2.3: Prior Plain Radiographs
Prior standing weight-bearing plain radiographs (minimum 3 views) must be completed prior to MRI request to rule out advanced osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4).

section_title: Section 2: Knee Magnetic Resonance Imaging (CPT-73721)
text:
Clause 2.4: Exclusion and Non-Covered Conditions
MRI is not authorized when plain radiographs demonstrate bone-on-bone tri-compartmental osteoarthritis unless acute osteonecrosis or surgical planning for unicompartmental arthroplasty is documented.

---

section_title: Section 3: Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography (CPT-75574)
text:
Clause 3.1: Clinical Indication Overview
Coronary CT Angiography (CCTA) (CPT-75574) is indicated for symptomatic patients with low-to-intermediate pre-test probability of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD).

section_title: Section 3: Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography (CPT-75574)
text:
Clause 3.2: Objective Baseline Testing Criteria
Authorization requires:
- Documented baseline 12-lead resting electrocardiogram (ECG) interpreted by a cardiologist.
- Low-to-intermediate CAD Consortium risk score or Diamond-Forrester score between 15% and 85%.
- Inconclusive or uninterpretable prior stress test (e.g. stress echocardiogram or treadmill exercise ECG).

section_title: Section 3: Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography (CPT-75574)
text:
Clause 3.3: Exclusions and Contraindications
CCTA is contraindicated and not authorized for:
- Asymptomatic screening in general population.
- Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m²).
- Extensive known coronary artery calcification (Agatston calcium score > 1000).

---

section_title: Section 4: General Denial & Appeal Governance
text:
Clause 4.1: Timely Appeal Filing Window
Standard first-level provider appeals must be received within sixty (60) calendar days of the initial denial notice date.

section_title: Section 4: General Denial & Appeal Governance
text:
Clause 4.2: Peer-to-Peer Review Window
Peer-to-peer discussion between the treating physician and medical director may be scheduled within fourteen (14) calendar days of initial denial.

section_title: Section 1: Lumbar Spine MRI (CPT-72148)
text:
Clause 1.1: Scope of Coverage
Unenhanced Lumbar Spine MRI (CPT-72148) is covered when persistent low back pain is accompanied by radiculopathy and non-operative therapy has proven unsuccessful.

section_title: Section 1: Lumbar Spine MRI (CPT-72148)
text:
Clause 1.2: Mandatory Step Therapy (Conservative Protocol)
Prior to approval, member must complete at least six (6) continuous weeks of comprehensive conservative management under clinical supervision within 6 months of the request date. Requirements include:
- Supervised active physical therapy (minimum 6 visits documented by PT clinic notes).
- Documented trial of prescription-strength oral anti-inflammatory or neuropathic pain medication.

section_title: Section 1: Lumbar Spine MRI (CPT-72148)
clause_title: Red Flag Exceptions (Exempt from Step Therapy)
text:
Clause 1.3: Red Flag Exceptions (Exempt from Step Therapy)
Pre-authorization is granted without conservative treatment when clinical notes document:
- Cauda equina syndrome with objective saddle sensory deficit.
- Acute or progressive lower extremity motor deficit (strength <= 3/5 on medical exam).
- Documented spinal fracture or suspected neoplasm.

section_title: Section 1: Lumbar Spine MRI (CPT-72148)
text:
Clause 1.4: Plain Radiograph Prerequisite
Standing anteroposterior (AP) and lateral lumbar spine X-rays performed within the prior 6 months must accompany the prior authorization submission.

---

section_title: Section 2: Knee MRI Without Contrast (CPT-73721)
text:
Clause 2.1: Meniscal and Ligamentous Injuries
Authorization requires physical examination indicating mechanical symptoms (catching, locking) or instability tests (positive Lachman or McMurray test), plus four (4) weeks of conservative treatment unless acute traumatic hemarthrosis is documented.

section_title: Section 2: Knee MRI Without Contrast (CPT-73721)
text:
Clause 2.2: Exclusion Criteria
Knee MRI is not approved in members over 50 years of age with known moderate-to-severe radiographic osteoarthritis in the absence of acute trauma or mechanical locking.

---

section_title: Section 3: Safety, Experimental & Off-Label Criteria
text:
Clause 3.1: Experimental and Investigational Technologies
Standing/weight-bearing positional MRI, upright MRI, or unapproved AI-only auto-adjudications are deemed experimental and investigational and are not eligible for coverage under this policy.

section_title: Section 3: Safety, Experimental & Off-Label Criteria
text:
Clause 3.2: Medical Necessity Ambiguity & Physician Escalation
When submitted clinical evidence contains contradictory neurological findings or when the clinical diagnosis does not align with standard ICD-10 indications, the request must be escalated to an independent physician reviewer (abstain from automated approval).

section_title: 3. Federal No Surprises Act — Your Rights and Protections Against Surprise Medical Bills
clause_title: What types of plans do these rights and protections apply to?
text:
What types of plans do these rights and protections apply to?
- Self-funded health benefit plans, including state government and municipal health benefit plans
- Fully insured health benefit plans
- Federal Employees Health Benefit Plan (FEHBP)
- Grandfathered Health Plans
- If you are not sure what type of plan you have, contact us — we're here to help you!

section_title: 3. Federal No Surprises Act — Your Rights and Protections Against Surprise Medical Bills
text:
What is "balance billing" (sometimes called "surprise billing")?
When you see a doctor or other health care provider, you may owe certain out-of-pocket costs, such as a copayment, coinsurance and/or a deductible. You may have other costs or must pay the entire bill if you see a provider or visit a health care facility that isn't in your health plan's network.

- **"Out-of-network"** describes providers and facilities that haven't signed a contract with your health plan. Out-of-network providers may be allowed to bill you for the difference between what your plan agreed to pay and the full amount charged for a service — this is **"balance billing."** This amount is likely more than in-network costs for the same service and might not count toward your annual out-of-pocket limit.
- **"Surprise billing"** is an unexpected balance bill. This can happen when you can't control who is involved in your care — for example, during an emergency, or when you schedule a visit at an in-network facility but are unexpectedly treated by an out-of-network provider.

section_title: 3. Federal No Surprises Act — Your Rights and Protections Against Surprise Medical Bills
clause_title: When balance billing isn't allowed, you also have the following protections:
text:
When balance billing isn't allowed, you also have the following protections:
- You are only responsible for paying your share of the cost (copayments, coinsurance, deductibles) that you would pay if the provider or facility was in-network. Your health plan will pay out-of-network providers and facilities directly.
- You're never required to give up your protections from balance billing. You also don't have to get care out-of-network — you can choose a provider or facility in your plan's network.

section_title: 3. Federal No Surprises Act — Your Rights and Protections Against Surprise Medical Bills
clause_title: You are protected from balance billing for:
text:
You are protected from balance billing for:
**Emergency services**
If you have an emergency medical condition and get emergency services from an out-of-network provider or facility, the most the provider or facility may bill you is your plan's in-network cost-sharing amount (copayments, deductibles, coinsurance). You **can't** be balance billed for these emergency services, including services you may get after you're in stable condition — unless you give written consent and give up your protections for post-stabilization services.

**Certain services performed by an out-of-network provider at an in-network hospital or ambulatory surgical center**
These out-of-network providers may not balance bill you or ask you to sign a written notice and consent form allowing balance billing. You pay only your plan's in-network cost-sharing amount. Applies to: anesthesia, assistant surgeon, emergency medicine, hospitalist, intensivist service, laboratory, neonatology, pathology, or radiology.

If you get **other services from any other out-of-network providers** at an in-network hospital or ambulatory surgical center, those providers **can't** balance bill you, unless you sign a written notice and consent form allowing balance billing and are provided a good faith cost estimate beforehand. **You are not required to sign the notice and consent form.** You may seek care from an available in-network provider.

**Air Ambulance**
When you receive medically necessary air ambulance services from an out-of-network provider, your cost share will be the same as if the service was provided in-network. Coinsurance/deductible will be based on in-network rates.

Some states have their own surprise bill/balance billing laws, which apply to fully insured plans and may affect some self-funded plans (state government, municipal, or church plans). Check with your plan administrator/booklet.

section_title: 3. Federal No Surprises Act — Your Rights and Protections Against Surprise Medical Bills
text:
Your health plan generally must:
- Cover emergency services without prior authorization
- Cover emergency services by out-of-network providers
- Base what you owe on in-network rates and show that in your EOB
- Count amounts you pay for emergency/out-of-network services toward your deductible and out-of-pocket limit

section_title: 4. Important Disclosure Information About Individual DMO Dental Plans (Generic)
clause_title: Features of a DMO dental plan
text:
Features of a DMO dental plan
Most, but not all, of the information in this document applies to your specific DMO dental plan. Some information applies only to a handful of states — check your Summary of Benefits plan documents, or call Member Services for a copy.

**Not yet a member?** Review the plan's Summary of Benefits and plan document to understand how a certain dental plan works.

**Avoid unexpected bills.** Check your plan documents to see what's covered *before* you get dental care, and get care from an in-network provider because:
- We have negotiated lower rates for you
- Network dentists won't bill you above our negotiated rates for covered services
- You have access to quality care from our national network

**Get a free printed directory.** Call the toll-free number on your member ID card, or **1-877-238-6200 (TTY: 711)** if you're not yet a member.

**Choose a primary care dentist (PCD).** Most DMO dental plans require you to select a PCD. If you don't pick one, your benefits may be limited or we may select one for you. Your PCD performs checkups/cleanings and refers you to specialists as needed. You don't need to call your PCD first in an emergency. You may change your PCD at any time.

section_title: 5. Important Disclosure Information About New York Individual DMO Dental Plans
clause_title: Features of a NY DMO dental plan
text:
Features of a NY DMO dental plan
**Understanding your plan of benefits.** Aetna DMO plans cover many, but not all, dental services. Check your Summary of Benefits and policy documents, or call Member Services at **1-877-238-6200 (TTY: 711)**.

**We check if it's medically necessary.** A service is deemed medically necessary only if it is:
- Clinically appropriate in type, frequency, extent, site, and duration, and effective for the condition
- Required for direct care/treatment/management of the condition
- Such that your condition would be adversely affected if not provided
- In accordance with generally accepted standards of dental practice
- Not primarily for convenience of you, your family, or your provider
- Not more costly than an equally effective alternative

**Utilization review.** Includes review before (predetermination), during (concurrent), or after (retrospective) service. Questions: call the number on your ID card (toll-free line available ≥40 hrs/week with after-hours machine). Determinations of "not medically necessary" are made by licensed dentists or similarly credentialed professionals.

**Referrals for in-network specialist care.** You need a referral from your PCD to see a network specialist. Referrals are valid once requested; your DMO plan provides timely access to in-network care.

section_title: 5. Important Disclosure Information About New York Individual DMO Dental Plans
clause_title: How we pay your dentist and other providers
text:
How we pay your dentist and other providers
A dentist's reimbursement combines the amount Aetna pays, the member's copay/coinsurance, and negotiated DMO provider rates. The DMO plan has **no deductibles or annual maximums**.

**Not yet a member? / Avoid unexpected bills / How to find an in-network provider / Get a free printed directory** — same guidance as above; provider search tool at Aetna.com; call **1-877-238-6200 (TTY: 711)**.

**Choose a primary care dentist (PCD)** — same as above.

**Why use in-network providers?** You pay less out of pocket; some plans don't cover out-of-network services at all, or require a larger out-of-network cost share.

**Choosing and changing network providers.** Change your PCD anytime via **1-877-238-6200 (TTY: 711)** or Aetna.com.

**Members with special communication needs.** Aetna uses Language Line for 24/7 interpretation in 200+ languages. EOBs and other correspondence note that translation services are available.

section_title: 5. Important Disclosure Information About New York Individual DMO Dental Plans
text:
Important Telephone Numbers and Addresses
- **Claims:** Aetna, P.O. Box 14094, Lexington, KY 40512-4094 (or address on your ID card)
- **Complaints, Grievances & Utilization Review Appeals:** 1-800-558-0860 (or number on ID card)
- **Member Services:** 1-877-238-6200 (Mon–Fri, 8am–6pm)
- **Website:** Aetna.com

**How to file a claim.** Network providers generally file for you; out-of-network claims may need to be filed by you or your provider within 24 months of service.

**Monitoring network quality / Access to Care.** Aetna measures geographic distribution of providers, member-to-practitioner ratios, complaints/surveys, and reviews underserved counties annually.

**Continuity of care.** Annual analyses of claim/referral data and member/provider experience surveys.

**Quality of care.** Dental Quality Management (QM) Program identifies and addresses quality concerns via complaints, surveys, utilization review, and credentialing issues; reviewed annually.

**How we build your network.** Providers are credentialed on licensure, DEA certification, academic background, certifications, sanction/malpractice history, malpractice insurance, access/availability, and cost efficiency — rechecked every 3 years. Ongoing monitoring includes state licensure sanctions, loss of license, OPM/OIG reports, and Medicare opt-outs.

section_title: 6. Member Handbook and Consumer Disclosure — Individual DMO Plans from Aetna Dental Inc. (Texas)
text:
Covered benefits
The plan does not cover all dental expenses. Through your PCD (directly or via referral, except emergencies) you access: visits/exams, X-rays/pathology, endodontics, restorations/repairs, periodontics, oral surgery, space maintainers, nutritional/tobacco counseling, and external bleaching.

**Emergency and urgent care.** An emergency is a sudden, severe condition (e.g., excessive bleeding, severe pain, acute infection) requiring immediate care.
1. If possible, call your PCD or Aetna Member Services first.
2. If not possible, call your closest dental provider.

Claims from non-PCD providers for emergency conditions are paid at usual/customary or agreed rates; you're responsible for the copay in your Dental Care Schedule. You may need to pay at time of service and submit the bill to Aetna yourself.

section_title: 6. Member Handbook and Consumer Disclosure — Individual DMO Plans from Aetna Dental Inc. (Texas)
text:
What you pay
**Out-of-network costs.** Aetna DMO is network-only — services from out-of-network dentists are your full responsibility unless pre-approved. You may request in-network-level benefits if no network dentist is available within 75 miles; Member Services can authorize an out-of-network dentist at in-network cost. Facility-based out-of-network providers at a network facility: you're held harmless and owe only normal copay/cost-share amounts.

**Financial responsibility.** You owe all applicable copayments/premiums (detailed in your enrollment kit) and the full cost of noncovered services. **Copayment** = fixed amount (e.g., $15) for a covered service.

**Notice:** You bear all costs for unauthorized care/drugs. Report balance bills via the number on your ID card. Aetna must pay non-network providers at usual/customary or agreed rates, with an EOB confirming this if no rate was agreed.

section_title: 6. Member Handbook and Consumer Disclosure — Individual DMO Plans from Aetna Dental Inc. (Texas)
text:
Exclusions and limitations
Not covered except as described in riders/amendments:
1. Services/supplies not covered by your plan documents
2. Treatment for non-occupational... *(services/supplies to diagnose or treat a disease/injury that is not a nonoccupational disease/injury)*
3. Services not listed in the Dental Care Schedule
4. Replacement of lost/missing/stolen appliances, or those damaged by abuse/misuse/neglect
5. Plastic/reconstructive/cosmetic surgery or appearance-altering services (except injury repair or congenital defects; facings on molar crowns/pontics always considered cosmetic)
6. Appliances/services used only for splinting, altering vertical dimension, restoring occlusion, or correcting attrition/abrasion/erosion
7. Services not meeting broadly accepted national standards of care (e.g., excessive same-visit scaling/root planing, unsupported treatment, inadequate treatment, prosthetics on severely compromised abutment teeth)
8. Medically necessary medical/surgical diagnosis or treatment of jaw joint disorders
9. Space maintainers (except for premature loss of deciduous teeth)
10. Orthodontic treatment (unless specified)
11. General anesthesia/IV sedation (unless specified and paired with another covered service)
12. Treatment by non-dentists (except scaling/cleaning/fluoride by a supervised licensed hygienist)
13. Crowns/cast/processed restorations unless for decay/traumatic injury (not fillable) or as an abutment
14. Pontics/crowns/restorations with high noble metals (unless specified)
15. Surgical removal of impacted wisdom teeth for orthodontic reasons only (unless specified)
16. Services needed solely in connection with noncovered services
17. Services with no evidence of pathology/dysfunction/disease (other than covered preventive services)
18. Services from a nonparticipating provider (except out-of-area emergency care)
19. Services related to armed forces service or government-mandated benefits (excludes government-employee plans or Medicaid); Medicare benefits don't affect this plan's benefits

*Exclusions don't apply where coverage is legally required.*

**Benefits after termination of coverage.** Services after termination aren't covered, except certain *ordered* items (inlays, onlays, crowns, removable bridges, cast/processed restorations, dentures, fixed bridgework, root canals) installed/delivered within 30 days of termination, if properly "ordered" beforehand (impressions taken, pulp chamber opened, or teeth fully prepared, as applicable). If your PCD's contract terminates, they'll continue treating you until you select/are assigned a new PCD.

**No coverage based on U.S. sanctions.** No benefits if you're a blocked person, travel to a sanctioned country, or your provider is blocked/in a sanctioned country. See Treasury.gov/resource-center/sanctions/Pages/default.aspx.

What happens if your dentist leaves the dental plan

section_title: 6. Member Handbook and Consumer Disclosure — Individual DMO Plans from Aetna Dental Inc. (Texas)
text:
Referrals
Your PCD refers you to specialists in-network (written/electronic, no paper needed). Key points:
- Get the referral before receiving care
- No referral needed for emergencies
- Missing a required referral may mean you pay the bill yourself
- New recommended treatment outside the referral scope needs a new referral
- Referrals valid 1 year (first visit within 90 days of issue)
- If no in-network specialist is available in your area, Aetna can approve an out-of-network referral

section_title: 6. Member Handbook and Consumer Disclosure — Individual DMO Plans from Aetna Dental Inc. (Texas)
clause_title: What to do if you disagree with us
text:
What to do if you disagree with us
**Definitions**
- **Aetna Member Services:** 1-877-238-6200 (TTY: 711)
- **Authorized representative:** someone you authorize to act for you in the complaint process
- **Benefits or coverage decision:** based on plan exclusions/limitations, not medical necessity
- **Complaint:** any oral/written dissatisfaction about Aetna's operations (excludes simple misunderstandings resolved by clarifying information)

**How to file a complaint**
Written complaints: Aetna Dental Inc. (DMO), PO Box 14597, Lexington, KY 40512

**Step 1:** Acknowledgement letter within 5 business days; investigation and written response within 30 calendar days. Emergency/urgent/life-threatening complaints are resolved within 1 business day (decision communicated verbally/electronically, resolution letter within 3 days). Reviews aren't expedited for already-provided services.

**Step 2:** If unsatisfied, request a Complaint Appeal Panel meeting in writing. Acknowledgement within 5 business days; you'll receive panel documentation, reviewer specializations, and panel member details at least 5 business days before the meeting. You may appear in person, by phone, or via representative, and may present testimony and question those who made the original determination. Panel decisions are issued within 30 calendar days of the appeal request, including TDI contact information.

**Emergency conditions and options.** Ongoing emergency/urgent/life-threatening appeals are resolved within 1 business day; Aetna can provide a same/similar-specialty review in lieu of a panel meeting.

**Additional member rights.** Right to bring civil action under ERISA Section 502(a), if applicable. Voluntary alternative dispute resolution (e.g., mediation) may be available via your local U.S. Department of Labor office and state insurance regulator.

**Texas Department of Insurance contact:**
PO Box 12030, Austin, TX 78711-2030
Phone: 1-800-252-3439 | Fax: 512-490-1007
Web: TDI.Texas.gov | Email: ConsumerProtection@tdi.texas.gov

section_title: 6. Member Handbook and Consumer Disclosure — Individual DMO Plans from Aetna Dental Inc. (Texas)
clause_title: Your rights with a Health Maintenance Organization (HMO) plan
text:
Your rights with a Health Maintenance Organization (HMO) plan
*Notice from the Texas Department of Insurance*

**Your plan.** Your HMO contracts with "contracted" (in-network) providers; your plan only pays for in-network care, with exceptions for emergencies, situations where you didn't choose the provider, and ambulance services.

**Your plan's network.** Must have adequate doctors/facilities ("network adequacy") so you don't travel too far or wait too long. File network-adequacy complaints with TDI at www.tdi.texas.gov or 800-252-3439.

**List of doctors.** Directory available at www.aetna.com or via the number on your ID card. If you relied on the directory and a chosen in-network provider turns out to be out-of-network, you may not owe the extra out-of-network cost.

**Bills for health care.** If you received out-of-network care at an in-network facility without choosing that provider, you won't pay more than your normal copay/coinsurance/deductible — this also applies to emergency care at an out-of-network facility or connected lab/imaging work. Contact your health plan about unexpected bills; more info at tdi.texas.gov.

text:
Member rights
Full list of rights/responsibilities: Aetna.com/individuals-families/member-rights-resources.html, or call **1-877-238-6200 (TTY: 711)**.

**We protect your privacy.** Aetna protects personal (identifying, financial, health) information — excludes publicly available plan information or de-identified reports. Aetna may share information within the company, with affiliates, and disclose it to doctors/dentists/pharmacies/hospitals/caregivers, other insurers, vendors, government departments, and third-party administrators (TPAs), all bound to keep it private. Uses include paying claims, coverage decisions, coordination of benefits, quality assessment, plan improvement, and audits — disclosed without permission where legally allowed; see the full privacy notice for details. You have a right to access your information and request corrections (with an appeal right if Aetna disagrees).

Providers are independent contractors, not Aetna agents; provider participation may change without notice. Aetna does not guarantee access to dental services.
